title: Slim OTLP proxy: KPI normalizer and Prometheus-friendly export for inference telemetry
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Problem: Our current ingestion surfaces receive a mix of OTLP metrics, custom inference KPI events, and ad-hoc Prometheus exports from different components (serving runtime, routing layer, cache). Downstream SLOs and dashboards rely on consistent label semantics and per-request attributions (model, variant, route, customer_tier), but we still see noisy cardinality and a proliferation of incompatible metrics shapes.

Goal: Build a lightweight OTLP proxy service that sits in front of the main metrics ingestion pipeline and performs: normalized KPI mapping, cardinality reduction for high-cardinality keys (KV cache ids, ephemeral tokens), deterministic per-request attribution augmentation (trace->metric stitching), and an optional Prometheus-compatible metrics export for legacy consumers. The proxy must be inexpensive to run (CPU/min memory), support flow control and dynamic sampling rules, and be transparent (no dropped legal/time-series data without logging).

Success criteria:
- Consistent KPI mapping for at least 10 canonical inference KPIs (latency_p50/p90/p99, tokens_generated, cache_hit_rate, request_size_bytes, model_load_time, kv_kv_cache_usage).
- 50% reduction in unique label cardinality for the top noisy label keys in the first month post-rollout.
- End-to-end 99th percentile additional latency added by proxy < 8ms at target load.
- Feature-flagged rollout, with ability to switch to pass-through mode and audit all normalized transformations.

Design decisions:
- Ingest: OTLP/gRPC and OTLP/HTTP receivers (same code-path) with optional TLS.
- Normalize: Declarative mapping config (YAML) that maps incoming metric/attribute names into canonical KPI names and label keys. Mappings support regex capture groups and value transformations (e.g., quantize durations, bucket sizes).
- Cardinality controls: whitelist/blacklist per-label, deterministic hashing for ephemeral ids (expose k-anonymized hash salted per-tenant), and top-k label truncation with telemetry about truncated values.
- Sampling: Deterministic sampling for low-priority requests (based on hashed request_id % N), and adaptive reservoir sampling for error/failure traces to ensure we keep anomalies.
- Stitching: Use incoming trace context (traceparent / OTLP span refs) to augment metric points with request-level attributes (route, model, pin_version). If trace missing, fall back to best-effort correlation using timestamp-range joins and caller IP header.
- Output: Forward normalized OTLP to central ingestion (existing telemetry gateway) and offer a Prometheus exposition endpoint for legacy dashboards; expose a debug /audit endpoint returning original->normalized mappings for recent samples (bounded window).

API / Config contract:
- Mapping config schema v1 (examples in /docs/observability/mapping-v1.yaml).
- Runtime flags: pass_through=true|false, sampling_rate=0.02, truncate_labels=true.

Implementation notes:
- Tech stack: Go for low-latency binary, use existing OTLP collector library for receivers/exporters. Keep dependency footprint small.
- Metrics: internal exporter emits proxy_latency_ms, normalization_transform_count, mapping_errors_total, truncated_label_count, forwarded_points_total, sampled_points_total.
- Observability: instrument with traces for all normalization decisions (span tags: rule_id, matched_regex, truncated).

Rollout plan:
1) Alpha: local cluster only, configuration locked, collect health and performance. (ETA 2 weeks)
2) Canary: route 5% of traffic from a single region and a non-critical customer. Monitor normalization diff metrics and dashboards.
3) Gradual ramp to 100% over 7 days if no regression.
4) Fallback: kill-switch route returns to pass_through without normalization.

Testing & QA:
- Unit tests for mapping translations and hashing determinism.
- Integration test harness that replays captured raw ingestion files and validates normalized output diffs.
- Performance bench: sustained 20k metrics/sec with 8ms median added latency target.

Security & privacy: store no raw sensitive payloads. Hash salts are tenant-scoped and rotated monthly; salts are stored in KMS. Audit log of any mapping that reduces a label to hashed form.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Where to host the proxy for private deployments (VPC vs sidecar)? Proposal: hosted API and Dedicated run as a regional service; Private customers can opt for sidecar deployment as an alternative.
- How aggressive should default cardinality reduction be? Start conservative (log high-cardinality labels but do not drop) then tighten by release.

Artifacts & links:
- Design spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/obs-proxy-spec
- Mapping schema examples (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/obs/mapping-v1.yaml
- PR (work-in-progress): https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/412

Next steps:
- (Marco) prototype mapping loader and one sample transform rule for latency histogram->p50/p90 aggregation.
- (Aisha) coordinate with Platform SRE on canary customers and circuit-breaker knobs.
- Schedule security review if private-deploy sidecar path selected.
